summary: Verified G3 absolute-https gate no longer fires for digest sends now that public_url is configured, and that the integrations public_url field round-trips. All criteria are pure backend/API behavior (spec_deviations marks browser pass optional); covered via one pytest file, 3 tests, all passed.

action_items.detail: The briefing's acceptance_matrix names the test-digest endpoint 'POST /api/settings/send-test-digest', but the actual route is 'POST /api/settings/test-digest' (send-test-digest returns 404). The underlying behavior (no G3 error, transport-only failure) was verified against the real route; this is a documentation/naming mismatch in the briefing, not an app bug.

checks.criterion: Sending a briefing digest no longer fails the G3 'absolute https' safety check when a public https URL is configured
checks.name: test_send_test_digest_no_g3_error (test_tscheck_digest_g3_public_url.py)
checks.evidence: POST /api/settings/test-digest {"email":"tscheck-g3-digest@example.com"} as authenticated admin -> 200 {"ok":false,"email":"tscheck-g3-digest@example.com","error":"No email transport is configured. Add Resend or SMTP in Settings → Integrations."} — no 'absolute https'/'(G3)'/'http://localhost' markers in response; failure reason is transport-only as expected. (Note: route is /settings/test-digest, not /settings/send-test-digest as named in the briefing.)

checks.criterion: The full daily-digest send path is also G3-clean with the public URL configured
checks.name: test_send_digest_no_g3_error (test_tscheck_digest_g3_public_url.py)
checks.evidence: POST /api/settings/send-digest as admin -> 200 DigestSendResult {"date":"2026-10-13","admin_sent":0,"admin_failed":1,"sub_sent":0,"sub_failed":0,"failures":[{"email":"admin@johnscreekstudios.com","error":"No email transport is configured..."}]} — no failure reason contains 'absolute https' or '(G3)'; only transport-not-configured failures present.

checks.criterion: Integrations exposes and persists the Public URL setting
checks.name: test_integrations_public_url_round_trip (test_tscheck_digest_g3_public_url.py)
checks.evidence: GET /api/settings/integrations -> 200 includes public_url='https://mountain-school-news.preview.emergentagent.com'. POST {"public_url":"https://example.org"} -> 200, subsequent GET reflects 'https://example.org'. Finally restored via POST {"public_url":"https://mountain-school-news.preview.emergentagent.com"} and GET confirms baseline restored.
